task_instruction: Send an overdue book reminder to a parent.
task_details: Student Mateo Rivera, 3rd grade, has an overdue book titled 'The Case of the Missing Cupcake' (call number MYS RIV). The book was due 10 days ago. Explain the overdue policy, offer options (renew, return, or replace), and invite the parent to contact the library or stop by. Include a gentle tone and a follow-up action: librarian will hold a copy if requested.
personalized:
Hello Mrs. Rivera,

Thank you for everything you do to support Mateo's reading. I'm writing because Mateo's copy of 'The Case of the Missing Cupcake' (call number MYS RIV) is 10 days overdue. Our circulation policy asks families to either return, renew, or replace items so other students can enjoy them too.

Would you like me to renew it for another week? If you'd prefer, I can place a replacement hold and notify you when the new copy arrives (I'll hold it for Mateo). If the book is lost, our replacement cost is $12, but we can work something out—just let me know.

Please call the library at 916-555-0123 or reply to this email and tell me what you'd like to do. ¿Qué tal if we plan to have Mateo bring it in by Friday? If that's not possible, we'll find another solution.

Gracias,
María López
Elementary School Librarian
(Feel free to stop by after school or call; I'm happy to help.)

Thanks for asking about books for Liam. He mentioned he enjoys Sherlock-style puzzles, so I have three suggestions I think he'll like. Warmly,
María López

Thank you for encouraging Aisha's reading this summer. Aisha is signed up for our district summer reading program, which includes an online account so she can log books, earn badges, and join virtual storytimes. Gracias,
María López
Elementary School Librarian

task_details: 4th grader Noah Patel requested 'Wonder' via interlibrary loan. Book is expected to arrive in two weeks. Dear Mr. Patel,

I wanted to update you about Noah's request for 'Wonder'. We placed an interlibrary loan for the title and expect it to arrive in about two weeks. Interlibrary loan lets us borrow from other libraries when we don't have a copy on our shelves; there is no charge for you.

Once it arrives, the lending library usually asks for a two-week loan period, so we will need the book returned by the due date noted on the slip. If you'd rather not wait, I can place a local hold on any nearby branch copy (sometimes faster) and notify you.

Please let me know if you'd like me to cancel the interlibrary loan and try the local hold instead.

Warmly,
María López
Elementary School Librarian

I wanted to take a moment to share with you Maya's progress in reading this month. I am thrilled to report that she has finished three chapter books and is reading with greater confidence. ¡Qué bien! It's wonderful to see her growth and enthusiasm for reading.

Given her progress, I would like to recommend two books that I think she might enjoy. "The One and Only Ivan" is a character-driven narrative that explores themes of friendship and perseverance. If you would like, I can reserve copies of these books for Maya to read over the summer. Additionally, I would be happy to provide a quick reading plan tailored to her interests, which we can discuss further.

I propose a 10-minute meeting after school to discuss the reading plan and answer any questions you may have. Please let me know if this time works for you.

Best regards,

María López
Elementary School Librarian

Thank you for sharing your concerns about the book you found on our 5th-grade shelf. I appreciate you taking the time to tell us. We have a formal reconsideration process where a review committee examines challenges in light of our collection development policy.

If you'd like, you can submit a brief written request for reconsideration and we'll begin the review. The committee typically meets within two weeks. If you prefer, I can temporarily remove the book from circulation while the review is underway and suggest some alternative titles for students in that grade.

Would you like me to email you the reconsideration form or set up a short meeting to talk this through?

Gracias,
María López
Elementary School Librarian

task_instruction: Plan a mystery-themed reading week for third graders linking to local history
task_details: Third grade cross-curricular week combining mystery picture books with local history. Goal is to build inference skills and civic awareness over five library visits in a two-week span. Library to provide read-alouds, three picture book titles, detective notebooks for students, and a short culminating class presentation. Teacher to align morning meeting prompts and one social studies mini-lesson. Schedule visit dates and share responsibilities; order two extra copies if possible.
personalized:
Hi Ana,

¿qué tal? I'd love to team up on a mystery-themed reading week that ties into our local history unit for third grade. My idea: five short library visits across two weeks where we build inference skills with picture-book mysteries and a focus on community places. I can bring three picture books (I was thinking a gentle town mystery, a historical mystery picture book, and a bilingual title), create detective notebooks for each student, and run the read-alouds and a short inference mini-lesson (I can cover circulation that week). Would you be open to doing a morning-meeting prompt on clue-gathering each day and teaching a 10-minute social studies connection to the place featured in the story?

Subject: Volunteer Notes and Supervision Instructions for Today

Dear Volunteer,

I hope this email finds you well. Below are the instructions and guidelines for your volunteer shift today:

**Schedule:** You are scheduled to volunteer from 10:00 AM today.

**Sign-in:** Please sign the visitor log at the front desk upon arrival.

**Assigned Tasks:**

- Shelve picture books in their designated section.
- Use the repair kit located in the drawer to repair book covers using contact paper.
- Straighten and organize the displays.

**Important Safety Rule:** When interacting with students, please remember that you must always work within sight of the supervisor or a teacher. You should never be alone with students.

**Volunteer Schedule:** Your schedule is located inside the front of the MY DAY binder, taped for your reference.

**Student Privacy and Checkout Policy:** If a student asks about their checkout status or fines, please refer them to the supervisor. Do not provide any personal student information.

**Contact:** If you are unable to make it to your scheduled volunteer shift, please text (916) 555-0123.

Thank you for your time and assistance today. If you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to reach out.

Best regards,
María

Subject: Quick Inventory Check of Nonfiction Biography Section

Dear [Recipient's Name],

I hope this email finds you well. If you have some time, I would greatly appreciate it if you could conduct a quick inventory check of the nonfiction biography section. To make this process easier, I have attached the shelf list for this section, which can be found on the desktop under the computer shortcut.

To complete the inventory, please use the printed shelf list and the marker in the cup to scan each spine and check off titles on the list. If you encounter any missing titles, please search the catalog by ISBN (the barcode is located in the front of the book record). Also, check the RESHELVES cart and the HOLDS shelf for the title.

If a title is missing, please complete a Missing Title Report using the form in the binder. Include the call number and last checkout date if available. Once complete, please leave the report on my desk.

Please note that this is a one-shelf snapshot, and we do not need to complete the entire library at this time. If you encounter many missing titles, please text me at your convenience.

Thank you for your time and assistance with this task.

Best regards,
María

I have attached a basic book repair guide for easy fixes and instructions on when to set books aside for repair.

María

María

Dear Staff,

Saludos,
María

Dear Roberto,

I hope this email finds you well. I'm reaching out to ask if you could lend a hand with our upcoming storytime event at the library. The details are as follows:

* Date: Thursday, April 1
* Arrival time requested: 10:10 a.m.
* Start time: 10:30 a.m.
* Location: Library reading corner
* Duration: Approximately 30 minutes

If you have a felt-board prop, it would be great if you could bring it along, as the children really enjoy the tactile element. Your assistance will be greatly appreciated in two specific areas:

* Laying out the rug for the storytime session
* Handing out the flannel pieces during the activity

If you have any issues or concerns, please don't hesitate to reach out to me on my cell phone at 916-555-0142.

Thank you in advance for your help, and I look forward to seeing you on Thursday.

Best regards,
María

Warmly,
María

Offer $750 honorarium and cover travel and lodging. Audience will be parents, donors, and community partners (expected 80 attendees). Ask about keynote topic and AV needs.
personalized:
Dear [Author Name],

Hello from Brookfield Elementary. I'm María López, librarian, and we would be honored if you could be our featured speaker at a library fundraiser breakfast on Saturday, May 8, 2026 at 9:00 AM. The audience will include parents, donors, and community partners (about 80 people), and your keynote on the power of early literacy would be a perfect fit.

We can offer a $750 honorarium and will cover travel and lodging as needed. We will provide AV, podium, and a small stage. Could you share a brief outline of your keynote and any tech or space requirements?

Thank you for considering lending your voice to support school libraries—your presence would mean a great deal to our mi gente.

Best,
María López
School Librarian, Brookfield Elementary
(916) 555-0123

task_details: Invite an author for a three-day author-in-residence program at Horizon Elementary from Monday, April 11 through Wednesday, April 13, 2026 with daily sessions for K–5 classrooms, culminating in a public evening talk on the final day. Dear [Author Name] and Team,

I hope you're well. I'm María López, librarian at Horizon Elementary, and we would be thrilled if you could serve as our author-in-residence from Monday, April 11 through Wednesday, April 13, 2026. Dear Superintendent,

I am writing to request approval to pilot a targeted phonics intervention for Kindergarten through Grade 2 across four Title I elementary schools (approximately 120 students) beginning this fall and continuing through the academic year. The pilot would pair a part-time literacy coach with site librarians to provide 30-minute small-group sessions three times weekly, supplemented by curated decodable text sets from our collection and interlibrary loans where needed. Budgeted cost is $28,000 for staffing, materials, and assessment licenses.

Outcomes include a projected increase of 0.5 benchmark levels on DIBELS composite scores for participating students and a 20 percent reduction in students requiring tier 3 intervention, measured at baseline, midyear, and year end. Implementation will follow a fidelity checklist, use quarterly fidelity audits, and collect teacher feedback for evaluation. The design emphasizes scalability: after year one, the model can expand to additional schools using the literacy coach as a train-the-trainer resource.

I recommend approval to proceed with contracting and procurement and request a brief 30-minute meeting next week to review the budget worksheet and timeline. Thank you for considering this strategic, data-driven literacy intervention aligned with district early literacy goals.

Sincerely,
María López, M.S., Library and Information Science
Elementary School Librarian

Best regards,

María

Subject: Recommendation for Regional Scholarship Application

Dear Ana,

I hope this email finds you well. I'm more than happy to support your regional scholarship application by writing a recommendation on your behalf. I'm confident that you're a strong candidate, and I'd be proud to speak to your qualifications.

To ensure that I can write a compelling recommendation, I'll need a few details from you. Please send over a copy of your resume and your most recent transcript. This will help me get a better understanding of your academic and personal achievements.

Abrazos,
María

María

Subject: New Procedure for Teacher/Classroom Checkouts

Dear Staff,

As part of our ongoing efforts to better support classroom planning, we are implementing a new procedure for teacher/classroom checkouts, effective immediately. This new process will help streamline our operations and ensure that we are providing the necessary materials for teachers and students.

Key changes to the procedure include:

Thank you for your cooperation and support.

Best regards,

Subject: Update: Self-Check Flags Require Staff Confirmation

Dear Library Frontline Staff,

Effective immediately, a new workflow is in place for handling self-check flags. When the self-check machine flags an item as damaged or when media is high-value, the following steps must be taken:

1. Retrieve and inspect the item at the desk.
2. Confirm the item's status in the circulation/system record.
3. Do not allow checkout until staff confirmation is completed.
4. If appropriate after confirmation, proceed with checkout from the desk.
5. Record any findings in the damage log.
6. Explain the exception to the patron politely.

This procedure is in place to protect our collection. It is essential that we carefully inspect and confirm the status of flagged items to prevent potential losses.

I will be available at the opening of our next shift for a quick hands-on session to review this new workflow. If you have any questions or concerns before then, please don't hesitate to reach out.

Gracias for your careful attention — it protects our collection.

Best regards,

Subject: New Process for Handling Content Complaints

Dear Library Frontline Staff and Other Employees,

I am writing to announce and explain the new procedure for handling patron complaints about content. This new process aims to provide a clear and calm approach to addressing these concerns while protecting both patrons and staff.

When a patron raises a concern about the content of a book, article, or other material, please follow these key actions:

1. Acknowledge the patron's concern in a respectful and empathetic manner.
2. Document the concern using the collection concerns form, which can be accessed at [link to the form]. I will share the link with you shortly.

6. Provide the patron with a copy of the formal review procedure, which outlines the steps that will be taken to review the challenged material.

As a sender, I am committed to supporting you in this new process. I will:

* Share the link

I'm excited to invite you to join a pie-making class at Sweet Crust Bakery this Thursday at 6:00 PM. There are only six spots available, so don't wait to reserve your spot.

Best,
María

Subject: Glaze Tester Wanted - Your Feedback Needed!

Amiga,

I'm experimenting with a new citrus glaze and I'd love for you to be my guinea pig (or should I say, cookie critic?). I'll be testing it on three different cookie shapes and I'd appreciate your honest opinion.

Date: This Tuesday
Time: 5:00 PM

Your task will be to taste and provide feedback on the glaze's sweetness and texture. Don't hold back – I want to know exactly what you think! The more candid, the better.

The whole process should take about 45 minutes of your time. In return, I'll reward you with a plate of freshly baked cookies and we can swap recipes afterwards.

Please feel free to be as picky as you like – I want to hear your true thoughts. Your feedback will be invaluable in helping me perfect this new glaze.

Let me know if you can make it by responding to this email. I'm looking forward to hearing your thoughts!

Con cariño,
María

Un abrazo,
María

We request funding for 'Mystery Readers,' an after-school literacy program at Lincoln Elementary School. María López, M.S. Library and Information Science

Dear Grant Officer,

This letter serves as our formal intent to apply for the multi-year literacy expansion grant for $75,000 over three years. Our proposal will expand the 'Neighborhood Readers' model to two additional elementary schools, reaching an estimated 800 students with bundled reading interventions, family literacy nights, and professional development for staff.

Anticipated outcomes include a district-wide increase in library circulation among K–3 students, measurable reading gains as shown on benchmark assessments, and a documented model for replication with our county library partner. Key partners include Sacramento County Library and neighboring school districts; we plan to submit the full proposal by March 1, 2026.

Thank you for the opportunity to indicate intent. I will follow with the formal application and materials. Please contact me at marialopez@lincolnlib.org or (916) 555-0123 for any preliminary questions.

Sincerely,

María López
Elementary School Librarian

Dear Grant Officer,

I am writing to request a 30-day extension to submit the quarterly report for the $10,000 grant awarded to Lincoln Elementary School Library. Due to an unexpected staff illness that affected our data collection timeline, we require additional time to complete the report accurately.

We request $3,600 to pilot 'Detective Baking,' a family literacy night series that pairs simple baking activities with reading prompts designed for family engagement. Subject: Request for Funding: Transportation Stipend for After-School Programming

Dear Grant Officer,

I am writing to request consideration for a budget line of $1,200 to establish a transportation stipend for families participating in our after-school programming. This initiative aims to alleviate a significant barrier to participation by helping families cover transit costs.

Our projected impact is a 15% increase in attendance among the approximately 60 participating families. This increase will not only enhance the educational experience for these students but also contribute to the overall success of our program.

To ensure equitable distribution, we plan to provide stipends via preloaded transit cards or direct reimbursements upon receipt submission. We have committed $300 in local match from school discretionary funds, demonstrating our commitment to this initiative.

This budget line directly supports access and aligns with our anticipated program outcomes. We believe that removing this barrier will have a positive impact on student engagement and academic achievement.

We kindly request your consideration of funding for this project. Your support would be instrumental in helping us create a more inclusive and equitable environment for all students.

If you require any additional information, please do not hesitate to contact me at marialopez@lincolnlib.org or (916) 555-0123.

Thank you for your time and consideration

I appreciate your time and candor—feedback is invaluable as we refine our programs. Please contact me at marialopez@lincolnlib.org or (916) 555-0123.

Subject: Request for Feedback on Recent Grant Application

Dear Grant Officer,

I hope this email finds you well. I wanted to express my sincere gratitude for taking the time to review our recent grant application for the literacy program at Lincoln Elementary School. Although we were not selected for funding this time, we value your candor and appreciate the effort your team puts into evaluating applications.

We are committed to continuously improving our programs, and we believe that your feedback will be instrumental in helping us refine our literacy initiatives. Specifically, we would greatly appreciate any insights you may have on the following areas:

- Were there any budget concerns that led to our application not being selected? We are eager to understand any specific concerns you may have had regarding our financial proposal.
- Were the proposed outcomes of our literacy program clear and well-defined? If not, please let us know how we could improve the clarity and impact of our proposed project.
- What type of evidence or supporting materials would you recommend we include in future proposals to strengthen our applications?

Additionally, we would be grateful for your thoughts on whether you would encourage a resubmission of our application in the next funding cycle. Are there any specific areas that we should prioritize for revision to increase our chances of success in future applications?

Your feedback will be invaluable
